segments: [the great] {OCR?} church of Kesum and the fifteen shrines that were in it.
And on two thousand wagons he transported their stones to rebuild [it], which the Romans had destroyed;
and he rebuilt it anew.
And the Arabs entered the land of the Romans and the seashore,
and they took a great captivity.
And in the year 1100 [789 AD],
Walid went out from the heresy of the Harurites [Kharijites],
and he gathered five thousand [men] and came to Nisibis.
And he killed the emir,
and plundered the merchants,
and took five zuzé from every Christian.
And when he had defeated the army of Abd al-Malik,
and killed the Arabs,
and cleared the roads of travelers,
Yazid met him with an army and killed him.
And in the following year, Harun went up from Baghdad and came to Callinicus to dwell in it;
and he enlarged it with buildings,
and planted in it a multitude of orchards.
And he brought out for it a canal from the Euphrates,
and another canal he brought from Sarug;
he bought the water of the villages of Sarug from their owners,
and dug for them a new canal.
And in the year 1104 [793 AD],
and many were killed.
And Abd al-Malik took a great captivity from the land of the Romans.
And his son Abd al-Rahman captured the fortress of Rapsa in Cappadocia;
and four hundred men died in it from thirst,
and then they surrendered it.
At this time, Emperor Constantine, when he wished to put out the eyes of Elpidius, Patrician of Sicily, because he committed adultery with his mother,
[Elpidius] fled to the Arabs.
And the Emperor commanded,
and also made the nobles swear,
that his mother should no longer be proclaimed Empress.
Elpidius, however, took forty thousand of the army of the Arabs with Emir Sulayman,
and they entered the district called Samison.
And winter overtook them,
and four thousand of them died;
and from their distress they took refuge with the Romans.
They, however, showed philanthropy [humanity],
and did not harm the Arabs.
And they came out in the Latter Kanun [January], while the feet of many were frostbitten {dissolved} in the snow.
And Mor Dionysius, the Patriarch of Tel-Mahre, says:
"I saw about four hundred men of them in Edessa."
And afterward Constantine was reconciled with Irene his mother,
and commanded that she should be proclaimed Empress.
